title: A vector for any type
description:
Write a growable array that stores copies of elements of any size:

```c
typedef struct { unsigned char *data; size_t len, cap, elem; } Vec;

Vec vec_new(size_t elem);                                      /* elem = size of one element */
int vec_push(Vec *v, const void *item);                        /* 0, or -1 if out of memory */
void *vec_at(const Vec *v, size_t i);                          /* NULL when i is out of range */
int vec_remove(Vec *v, size_t i, void *out);                   /* copies the element to out (if not NULL), closes the gap; 0 or -1 */
void vec_sort(Vec *v, int (*cmp)(const void *, const void *));
void vec_free(Vec *v);
```

Remove must keep the order of the remaining elements (use `memmove`, since the areas overlap).
hints: Element `i` lives at `v->data + i * v->elem`; every function is built on that one formula (lesson 8.02).
To close the gap after element `i`, move the `len - i - 1` elements after it one place down with `memmove`.
